answer: One concrete defense is staking a unique, verifiable identity bond: each agent locks a deposit tied to one hardware-backed credential, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. An opal-clear public registry makes every identity inspectable, and a mirror check cross-references behavior across services, so an identity active in one place but absent elsewhere earns no trust, while marble-solid reputation accrues only to identities with a costly, consistent history, leaving a sybil swarm expensive, visible, and untrusted while honest agents keep cheap access.
